name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder-width.
Let the bar hang at arm's length against your thighs, elbows tucked close to your sides and shoulders back.
Curl the bar upward by flexing at the elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary, until the bar reaches shoulder height.
Squeeze the biceps briefly at the top without swinging the torso.
Lower the bar slowly under control back to the starting position, fully extending the elbows.
formCues: Keep elbows pinned to your sides throughout
Move only at the elbow, not the shoulders or back
Control the lowering phase for 2-3 seconds
commonMistakes: Using momentum and swinging the hips to heave the weight up
Letting the elbows drift forward at the top
Bouncing the bar at the bottom instead of lowering under control

name: Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Stand or sit upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, palms facing your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your shoulders back and down.
Curl one or both dumbbells upward, rotating your wrists so the palms face up (supinate) as you lift.
Continue until the dumbbells are near shoulder level and squeeze the biceps.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to full extension, reversing the wrist rotation.
formCues: Supinate the wrist as you curl for a full biceps contraction
Keep upper arms still and elbows by your sides
Lower under control without dropping the weight
commonMistakes: Swinging the body to generate momentum
Allowing the elbows to flare out or drift forward
Using too heavy a weight and shortening the range of motion

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your elbows tucked to your sides and arms fully extended at the start.
Curl the dumbbells upward while maintaining the neutral, thumbs-up grip throughout.
Raise until the dumbbells reach shoulder height and pause briefly.
Lower the dumbbells slowly and under control back to full extension.
formCues: Maintain a neutral grip for the entire rep
Keep wrists straight and elbows fixed at your sides
Control the descent rather than letting gravity drop the weight
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to lift heavier weight
Letting the elbows drift forward or flare out
Rushing the eccentric portion of the rep

name: Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench and adjust the seat so the top of the pad sits just under your armpits.
Rest the backs of your upper arms flat on the angled pad and grip an EZ bar with an underhand grip.
Start with the arms nearly extended, keeping a slight bend at the elbow to protect the joint.
Curl the bar upward by flexing the elbows until your forearms are near vertical.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly until the arms are almost fully extended.
formCues: Keep the backs of your arms pressed into the pad
Avoid fully locking out and hyperextending at the bottom
Lower with a slow, controlled tempo
commonMistakes: Letting the arms snap into full extension at the bottom
Lifting the elbows off the pad to cheat the weight up
Using too much weight and dropping the bar on the descent

name: Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat and spread wider than hip-width.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and brace the back of that upper arm against the inside of your thigh.
Let the dumbbell hang at arm's length with your palm facing inward toward the opposite leg.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder by flexing only at the elbow, supinating slightly as you lift.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top, then lower slowly back to full extension.
formCues: Keep the upper arm braced against your thigh and still
Squeeze at the top for a strong peak contraction
Move only at the elbow, isolating the biceps
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbell up using shoulder or back movement
Not achieving full extension at the bottom
Rushing reps instead of controlling the lowering phase

name: Cable Curl
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ bar to a low cable pulley and grip it with an underhand grip.
Stand upright a step back from the machine with feet shoulder-width and elbows tucked to your sides.
Start with the arms extended and the cable under tension at the bottom.
Curl the bar upward toward your shoulders by flexing at the elbows, keeping the upper arms still.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension while maintaining cable tension.
formCues: Keep constant tension on the cable throughout the rep
Pin your elbows to your sides and move only at the elbow
Resist the cable on the way down for a controlled eccentric
commonMistakes: Leaning back or using body sway to move the weight
Letting the stack slam and losing tension at the bottom
Allowing the elbows to drift forward at the top

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to roughly a 45-60 degree incline and sit back against it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down behind your torso, palms facing forward.
Keep your back against the pad and your upper arms stationary throughout.
Curl both dumbbells upward by flexing at the elbows until they reach shoulder level.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch at the bottom.
formCues: Let the arms hang back to maximize the biceps stretch
Keep your shoulder blades and back on the bench
Control the eccentric to take advantage of the stretched position
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows swing forward to shorten the range
Lifting the back off the bench to cheat the weight
Using excessive weight and losing the deep stretch
